arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Landau argued that the parties agree mixed cases can go to district court.
Mr. Fletcher argued that the Federal Circuit generally has exclusive jurisdiction over Board decisions.
Mr. Fletcher noted that a specific statute carves out an exception for mixed cases.
Mr. Landau stated that the relevant agency interprets the statute similarly to the side that brought the case's view.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case involves a federal employee who claims discrimination and an adverse civil service action. The core legal question is whether the employee must exhaust internal discrimination remedies before filing suit in federal district court.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case determines the procedural path for federal employees alleging discrimination and adverse actions. It defines when district courts gain jurisdiction over mixed civil service cases. The outcome shapes the balance between agency review and judicial access for federal workers.
